messages:
sam: Hey team, shipping my first PR touching runtime/config. Quick onboarding Qs: do we prefer atomized commits (one per logical step) or a single squashed commit on merge? also what branch prefix should I use?

ella: congrats! we like to keep history readable: craft small, focused commits while developing, but squash noisy WIP commits before merge. The final commit should follow Conventional Commits.

rio: Branches: feature work -> feature/<yourname>/short-desc, bugfixes -> fix/<short-desc>, urgent production fixes -> hotfix/<ticket>. Example: feature/sam/kv-prefetch-opt

sam: thanks. any strict rules on commit message format?

ella: yes, subject line pattern: <type>(<scope>): <short description>. scope is optional but helpful (eg runtime, api). Keep subject <= 72 chars. Body: 1-2 lines why + testing notes. Example:

```
feat(runtime): add kv prefetch for short sequences

Prefetch avoids repeated disk lookups for short requests, improving p95 latency by ~6%.
Test: unit + integration smoke. Resolves #456.
```

ci-bot: redwood-ci: lint, tests, typecheck started for PR #367; status: running. Details: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/367

sam: awesome. PR size? How big is too big?

rio: aim < 300 LOC if possible. If the change is bigger, split into a pure refactor/prep PR then feature PR. That makes reviews faster.

ella: Also add a concise "how to validate" section in the PR body and include commands to run locally. Use headings: What, Why, How to test, Rollout.

sam: pre-commit hooks — run locally?

rio: yes, run `pre-commit run --all-files` and `pytest tests/unit -q`. Formatting tools: `ruff format` and `black .`. We have a Git hook that runs some checks but run them locally to save CI cycles.

devex-bot: Tip: See repo docs at /CONTRIBUTING.md and /STYLE.md. PR template auto-populates checklist when you open a PR.

sam: Where do CODEOWNERS live? Want to make sure right people get pinged.

ella: CODEOWNERS at .github/CODEOWNERS. For runtime it will request @eng-runtime and any file-level owners. If you touch customer-facing APIs add @product-apis.

sam: If CI fails after merge, what's the preferred action? revert or patch forward?

rio: Prefer patch forward for non-urgent breakage. If it impacts production SLAs open a revert and escalate to eng-sre oncall. For release branch issues use hotfix branch and cherry-pick.

sam: any note about changelog?

ella: We auto-generate release notes from Conventional Commits, but add a manual entry in docs/changelog.md for behavioral changes or deprecations.

sam: one last nit: how do I do an interactive rebase safely before force-push?

rio: rebase flow we recommend:
```
git fetch origin
git rebase -i origin/main
# squash or reword as needed, then
git push --force-with-lease
```

If you're unsure, open a draft PR and ask for a rebase review.

sam: perfect, thanks! I'll run the hooks and ping @ella when ready for a quick review. :pray:

ella: happy to! small suggestion: include a tiny benchmark if it touches perf-critical paths. Otherwise quick LGTM. :rocket:
